message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  NODE_VERSION: 22
  JAVA_VERSION: 21

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: macos-15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Node.js ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
      - name: Set up Java ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: "zulu"
          java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Build iOS
        run: npm run verify:ios
      - name: Build Android
        run: npm run verify:android
      - name: Build Web
        run: npm run verify:web
      - name: Build Electron
        run: npm run verify:electron
      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dist
          path: dist
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: macos-15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Node.js ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Run Lint script
        run: npm run lint",
  "rationale": "Add npm dependency caching via setup-node's cache option to both jobs. The workflow runs npm ci on every push/PR without caching, and package-lock.json exists as a cache input. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE evidence supports caching dependency downloads with modest VM time reduction; preconditions (repeated dependency fetching, lockfile input) are met and no contraindications apply. All build and test steps are preserved.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
